description:
Point any app or device that already speaks SMTP at the gateway and relay through a server you control to recipient addresses you fix in advance — the platform authenticates each call with your UnitySVC API key (used as the SMTP password) and forwards it to your upstream, without ever storing your messages. Mail always goes to the recipients you configured, whatever addresses the sender names, so it can also be your `email` preference: a copy of everything sent to you through the `email` service, delivered to another address through your own server.

Multi-channel: the free `byok` channel relays every call to one SMTP server you store once as customer secrets, while the metered `plus` channel runs many relays under a single account — each enrollment binds its own host/port/username plus a named password secret and is reached at a unique `/e/<code>` address. See “How to use this service” for both channels.
name: smtp-relay

payout_price.description: No platform commission — customer uses own SMTP

summary: Bring Your Own Key SMTP relay: send email through the UnitySVC gateway via your own mail server (Gmail, SES, SendGrid, …). You bring the key; the platform handles auth, routing, and metering.

host.description: SMTP host (default: mailpit.unitysvc.dev — the platform's mailpit testing sink, accepts any mail without authentication). For production: smtp.gmail.com, smtp.sendgrid.net, email-smtp.us-east-1.amazonaws.com, etc.

password_secret.description: Name of the customer secret holding the SMTP password (app-password / API key). Defaults to `SMTP_RELAY_PASSWORD` — the name the free `byok` channel uses — so empty-params enrollments share the seller-seeded testing secret. Override to a per-enrollment name to bind a different key.

port.description: SMTP port (default: 1025 for mailpit; 587 for STARTTLS; 465 for TLS).

tls.description: Whether to issue STARTTLS on the upstream connection (default: false for the mailpit testing sink). Set true for real SMTP providers (Gmail, SendGrid, SES).

to.description: Recipient address(es) this enrollment delivers to, comma-separated for several (e.g. `me@work.example.com`). Mail always goes here, whatever recipients the sender names, so the relay can't be used to reach arbitrary addresses.

username.description: SMTP username (default: empty for mailpit; usually your sending address or an API username).
